title: A4 gaps: goroutine panics, a broken stderr silencing run.log, and a racy pidfile claim
description:
Three holes in the A4 liveness story, found by reading the code during the h0f review and NOT reproduced - verify each before repairing:

1. The recover at cli.go:386-397 covers only the main goroutine. A panic on any other goroutine leaves no cause and no run_died event, which is exactly the silence run_died exists to prevent.
2. io.MultiWriter(stderr, log) at cli.go:367 stops writing run.log once stderr is broken - a redirected or closed terminal takes the durable log with it.
3. Claim (runlife.go:88-105) is check-then-rename with no exclusion, so two run-epic processes racing can both believe they hold the run.

Each is small on its own; together they are the difference between 'the run died and said so' and 'the run vanished'.

Found by the h0f Phase 3 review.
acceptance_criteria: A panic on a non-main goroutine still produces a cause and a run_died event. run.log keeps receiving output when stderr fails. Two processes racing to claim one run cannot both win, proven by a test that runs the race.
